stem: Best guess: which shareholder would make a corporation ineligible for S status?

choices.explanation: Individuals who are citizens are eligible.
Correct. Partnerships and corporations can't be S corporation shareholders.

explanation: Partnerships and corporations can't be S corporation shareholders.

stem: A shareholder has stock basis of $10,000 and has loaned the S corporation $8,000. His share of the loss is $(25,000). How much can he deduct?

choices.explanation: Limited to stock plus debt basis.
Correct. Losses reduce stock basis, then debt basis; $7,000 is suspended.

explanation: Losses reduce stock basis, then debt basis; $7,000 is suspended.

stem: An S corporation with accumulated E&P distributes more than its AAA. The portion from accumulated E&P is:

choices.explanation: Capital gain arises only after basis is exhausted.
Correct. §1368(c): AAA first, then accumulated E&P as a dividend.

choices.text: Ordinary income subject to SE tax

explanation: §1368(c): AAA first, then accumulated E&P as a dividend.

stem: A calendar-year corporation wants S status for 2025. By what date must Form 2553 be filed?

choices.explanation: Correct. The deadline is 2 months and 15 days after the start of the tax year (March 15), but March 15, 2025 is a Saturday, so it moves to Monday, March 17 (IRC §7503).

explanation: Form 2553 is due within 2 months and 15 days after the start of the tax year the election is to take effect (March 15 for a calendar year). March 15, 2025 falls on a Saturday, so under IRC §7503 the deadline is Monday, March 17, 2025.

stem: Which feature violates the one-class-of-stock requirement?

choices.text: Shares with different rights to liquidation proceeds
choices.explanation: Correct. All shares must have identical rights to distribution and liquidation proceeds.

choices.text: A buy-sell agreement at book value
Straight debt owed to a shareholder
choices.explanation: Straight debt is a safe harbor.

explanation: All shares must have identical rights to distribution and liquidation proceeds.

stem: An S corporation shareholder's beginning stock basis is $40,000. Share of ordinary income $25,000; tax-exempt income $3,000; nondeductible expenses $1,000; distributions $30,000. What is ending stock basis?
explanation: Increase for all income (including tax-exempt), then decrease for distributions and nondeductible expenses.

stem: A shareholder personally guarantees a $100,000 bank loan to her S corporation. How does the guarantee affect her basis?

choices.text: No effect unless she pays on the guarantee
choices.explanation: Correct. Debt basis arises only from loans the shareholder makes directly to the corporation.

choices.text: Increases basis by her ownership share
choices.explanation: Unlike partnerships, S corporation debt isn't shared.

explanation: Debt basis arises only from loans the shareholder makes directly to the corporation.

stem: A C corporation converted to S status on January 1, 2023, when an asset's FMV was $100,000 and basis $40,000. In 2025 it sells the asset for $120,000. What gain is subject to the built-in gains tax?

choices.explanation: Limited to built-in gain at conversion.
Correct. Recognized built-in gain = FMV at conversion − basis = 60,000; taxed at 21%.

explanation: Recognized built-in gain = FMV at conversion − basis = 60,000; taxed at 21%.

stem: When does an S election terminate because of excess passive investment income?

choices.text: In the first year passive income exceeds 25% of gross receipts
After 3 consecutive years of excess passive income while having accumulated C-corporation E&P
choices.explanation: Correct. §1362(d)(3): 3 consecutive years with E&P and passive investment income over 25% of gross receipts.
The threshold is 25% for 3 years with E&P.

choices.text: Never — S corporations can earn any type of income

explanation: §1362(d)(3): 3 consecutive years with E&P and passive investment income over 25% of gross receipts.

stem: Shareholders owning 60% of the shares consent to revoke the S election on February 1, 2025 without specifying a date. When is the revocation effective?

choices.explanation: A revocation made by the 15th day of the 3rd month is retroactive to the year's start.
Correct. A revocation made on or before the 15th day of the 3rd month is effective for the entire current year.

choices.text: It isn't effective — unanimous consent is required

explanation: A revocation made on or before the 15th day of the 3rd month is effective for the entire current year.

stem: Two owners split S corporation shares 50/50 until one sells half her shares to a new shareholder on July 1 (mid-year). How is the year's income allocated (no election)?

choices.explanation: Correct. §1377(a): per-share, per-day allocation unless the closing-of-the-books election is made.

choices.text: 50/50 because that was the ownership on January 1

choices.explanation: Year-end ownership isn't the default rule.
S corporations can't make special allocations.

explanation: §1377(a): per-share, per-day allocation unless the closing-of-the-books election is made.

stem: An S corporation shareholder-employee takes no salary and $200,000 of distributions from a profitable business. What is the main risk?

choices.text: The distributions are taxed as dividends
choices.explanation: Without E&P they aren't dividends; the real risk is recharacterization.

choices.text: The IRS may recharacterize part as wages subject to payroll tax
choices.explanation: Correct. Shareholder-employees must be paid reasonable compensation.
BIG tax relates to converted C corporation assets.

explanation: Shareholder-employees must be paid reasonable compensation.

stem: An S corporation that was never a C corporation distributes $70,000 to its sole shareholder, whose stock basis is $50,000. What is taxable?

choices.explanation: Correct. Without E&P: tax-free up to basis, excess is gain from sale of stock.

explanation: Without E&P: tax-free up to basis, excess is gain from sale of stock.

stem: Kai owns an S corporation. On January 1, Kai's stock basis was $10,000 and his debt basis from a direct loan was $8,000. Kai also guarantees a $25,000 bank loan to the corporation. His share of this year's items is $3,000 of tax-exempt interest and a $20,000 ordinary loss. The preparer's schedule shows ending debt basis of $23,000. What is the correct ending debt basis?

choices.explanation: Correct. Stock basis 10,000 + 3,000 = 13,000 absorbs the first 13,000 of loss; the remaining 7,000 reduces the 8,000 debt basis to 1,000. The guarantee creates no basis.
This is the preparer's figure, which counts the guarantee as debt basis.
This leaves out the tax-exempt interest, which increases stock basis.
Losses exceeding stock basis reduce debt basis.

explanation: Only direct shareholder loans create debt basis, and tax-exempt income increases stock basis before losses are applied.

stem: An S corporation with AAA of $30,000 and accumulated E&P of $20,000 distributes $40,000 to its sole shareholder, whose stock basis is ample. If it makes the election to distribute AEP first, how does the shareholder's dividend income change?

choices.explanation: The dividend without the election is 10,000, not zero.
The election changes the ordering and so the amount taxed as a dividend.
Distributing AEP first increases, not decreases, dividend income.
Correct. Without the election: 30,000 from AAA, then a 10,000 dividend. With it: a 20,000 dividend first, then 20,000 from AAA — 10,000 more dividend income.

explanation: The §1368(e)(3) election trades higher current dividend income for eliminating AEP, which removes the passive-income tax and termination exposure.

stem: An S corporation that was never a C corporation distributes $15,000 to a shareholder with a $10,000 stock basis. What is the result?

choices.explanation: Correct. The excess over basis is gain.
The excess over basis is gain.

explanation: Distributions from an S corporation without E&P reduce basis; any excess is capital gain.

stem: An S corporation shareholder sells all her shares on June 30. How is the year's income allocated?

choices.explanation: Correct. Unless all affected shareholders elect to close the books.
That isn't how the rule works.

explanation: S corporation items are allocated per share, per day, unless an election to close the books is made.

stem: An S shareholder's beginning basis is $10,000. Her share of income is $5,000, she receives a $12,000 distribution, and her share of a separately stated loss is $6,000. How much of the loss is deductible?

choices.explanation: Basis is limited after the distribution.
Correct. Income, then distributions, then losses.

explanation: Basis is increased by income ($15,000), reduced by distributions ($3,000), then by losses: $3,000 allowed, $3,000 suspended.

stem: An S corporation has accumulated E&P from C years, and passive investment income is 40% of gross receipts. What applies?

choices.text: No tax at the entity level

explanation: An S corporation with C-corporation E&P and passive investment income over 25% of gross receipts pays tax on excess net passive income.

stem: A calendar-year S corporation's election terminates on June 1 when a partnership buys shares. How is the year treated?

choices.explanation: The S year runs to May 31.
That isn't what the rule says.

choices.text: Split into S and C short years
choices.explanation: Correct. The C year starts June 1.

explanation: On termination, the year splits into an S short year ending the day before and a C short year beginning on the termination date.

stem: A C corporation using LIFO elects S status. What happens to its LIFO reserve?

choices.text: It's taxed in the final C year
choices.explanation: Correct. The tax is payable over 4 years.

choices.text: It's deducted in the first S year

explanation: §1363(d): the LIFO reserve is included in the C corporation's final-year income, with the tax payable in 4 installments.

stem: After an S election terminates, the corporation distributes cash during the post-termination transition period. How is it treated?

choices.text: Tax-free, up to AAA and basis

choices.explanation: That isn't what the rule says.

explanation: Cash distributions during the post-termination transition period are applied against AAA and treated as tax-free to the extent of basis.

stem: Who must consent to an S election on Form 2553?
explanation: All shareholders at the time of the election must consent.

stem: A former C corporation had a $300,000 net unrealized built-in gain at conversion. In Year 2 it sells an asset with a $120,000 built-in gain; its taxable income limit is $100,000. What is the built-in gains tax?

choices.explanation: Only recognized built-in gain is taxed.
Correct. Tax on the lesser of recognized built-in gain or taxable income; $20,000 carries forward.

explanation: The BIG tax is 21% × the lesser of net recognized built-in gain or taxable income; the excess carries forward.

stem: An S corporation has AAA of $30,000, accumulated E&P of $20,000 and OAA of $10,000. It distributes $70,000 to its sole shareholder (ample stock basis). How much is a dividend?

choices.explanation: Correct. Distributions come from AAA, then E&P, then OAA, then basis.

explanation: Ordering: AAA ($30,000) tax-free, E&P ($20,000) dividend, then OAA and basis.

stem: An S corporation with C-corporation E&P has passive investment income above 25% of gross receipts for 2023, 2024 and 2025. What happens?

choices.text: Nothing, if it distributes the E&P later

explanation: An S election terminates at the start of the year after 3 consecutive years of excess passive income with E&P.
